newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria tells freed Islamist leader "no politics".
newsitem.headline: Algeria tells freed Islamist leader "no politics".

text.p: Algeria on Friday ordered newly freed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) leader Abassi Madani to refrain from political activity, the interior ministry said in a statement.
Madani, who was freed on parole from prison last Tuesday halfway through a 12-year sentence imposed in 1992, has since been meeting former aides and making statements to journalists.

The ministry said in a statement that Madani was notified on Thursday that he "should abstain from making statements, verbal or writing, to national or foreign media as well as from taking part in meetings or public events that still require prior authorisation from the interior minister".
Madani said on Thursday he and his supporters would do all they could to end the violence that had shaken Algeria for more than five years.

Speaking to journalists on Thursday as he headed from an Algiers mosque to his parents' home in Belcourt, central Algiers, the leader of the outlawed FIS said: "We are going to do all we can to end this situation."
Madani had insisted that his release was "only justice".
But the ministry denied Madani's claims that he had won complete freedom in speech and movement and ordered him to respect the conditions of the rules for his release.

"Following numerous and repeated statements made by Abassi Madani since his release, the interior minister (Mustapha Ben Mansour) has issued an order reminding the concerned of his obligations under conditional release status," said the statement reported by the official Algerian news agency APS.
Madani was arrested in June 1991 and sentenced a year later by a military court to 12 years in jail for threatening the North African country's security. He was set free halfway through sentence.
About 60,000 people have been killed in the conflict between the government and the Islamists since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which FIS had taken a commanding lead.
